key_insight: Freya-TTS is a compact, Turkish-first text-to-speech model that aims to generate highly reliable conversational speech efficiently. Its main idea is to move speech generation into a frozen audio latent space, so the model can focus on mapping text to high-quality speech representations rather than predicting audio directly.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the need for a fast, compact, and dependable TTS system for Turkish speech synthesis, especially for conversational use cases. It targets the challenge of producing natural speech with high fidelity while keeping the model efficient and tokenization-free.
method: Uses a 183.2M-parameter non-autoregressive conditional flow-matching Diffusion Transformer (DiT).
Generates in the frozen continuous latent space of AudioVAE2, using 16 kHz encoding and 48 kHz decoding for high-quality reconstruction.
Avoids text tokenization, focusing model capacity on direct text-to-latent mapping for more efficient and robust synthesis.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, Freya-TTS shows a practical path to building smaller, more efficient TTS systems without sacrificing audio quality. Its tokenizer-free, latent-space design could simplify deployment and improve reliability for real-world conversational speech applications.
